I have been farming these 5 mu for 25 years, ever since I married into this village. My man works in the county town and sends back some money, but it is not much, so I have to watch every yuan I spend on the fields. Last year my wheat gave me about 900 jin per mu and the maize gave about 1,100 jin. I want to keep that this year, maybe a little more if the weather helps. I do not have much schooling, but I know my own land, and I watch what Sister Wang and the others on my lane do. If their wheat looks green and thick, I copy them.

The wheat is already in the ground from last autumn. I sowed improved seed, the kind the dealer in town sells, about 15 kg per mu. When I planted, I put down one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that is 50 kg per mu — and worked it in with the rotary tiller. I will topdress with half a bag of urea per mu, about 25 kg, when the wheat starts jointing in spring. Some people say that is too much, but two years ago I cut back and the ears came out small, so I will not make that mistake again. I would rather waste a little fertilizer than lose a whole harvest. I will irrigate three times if the spring stays dry: once around Qingming to wake the wheat up, once at jointing, and once at flowering. The pump costs electricity, but I would rather pay that than watch the crop turn yellow. For sprays, I do herbicide once in early spring, insecticide once when I see aphids, and if the weather turns wet and rust shows up, I will add fungicide — three times in total. I expect about 450 kg per mu.

For the summer maize, I will plant right after wheat harvest in early June. The gap is short, so I will not plough deep. I will do a quick pass or just plant directly with the hybrid seed I buy from the dealer — Deng hai or something like that, about 2.5 kg per mu. I will put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and when the maize is knee-high I will spread another 15 kg of urea per mu. That is what I did last year and it worked. I will irrigate twice: once if it is dry when the maize is about waist-high, and once at tasseling, because if the maize dries out when it is flowering, the cobs will be half empty. I spray herbicide once after planting and insecticide twice for the corn borers, so three times total. I hope to get 520 kg per mu.

I thought about buying more fertilizer because the dealer always pushes it, but with my daughter still in school and the pump repairs I had to do last month, I cannot stretch further. Five mu is not big — every bag of fertilizer is a real expense — so I will stick to what I know.
